docs.title: ocsf-schema-go
docs.text:
Go bindings and tooling for the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF).

The OCSF schema is authored in OCSF's own metaschema format — not standard JSON Schema. Event classes and objects declare partial attribute maps whose types live in a shared dictionary, inherit via extends, and mix in profile attributes via $include. This module compiles that format and generates idiomatic Go from it.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
Package Purpose ocsf/events Generated structs for every OCSF event class, plus constants, caption maps, and the class-UID registry (NewEventByClassUID, UnmarshalEvent) ocsf/objects Generated structs for every OCSF object, plus observable type registries ocsf/ocsfdata Generated embedded compiled schema for runtime access with no OCSF checkout validate Semantic validator: required attributes (profile-aware), types, enums, constraints, UID consistency recordintegrity record_integrity profile crypto: JCS canonicalization, fingerprints, signing (ECDSA/RSA), verification, tamper-evident chains schema Loads and compiles an OCSF source tree (extends, $include, dictionary types, platform extensions) gen / cmd/ocsfgen Code generator and its CLI ocsfext/integrity Schema extension adding digital_signature.signature_value (interim; see Upstream)

Bindings are generated from OCSF 1.10.0-dev, including the win, linux, and macos platform extensions.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import (
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/events"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/ocsf/ocsfdata"
    "github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/validate"
)

// Typed events with generated constants
evt := events.Authentication{
    ClassUID:    events.ClassUIDAuthentication, // 3002
    CategoryUID: events.CategoryUIDIAM,
    ActivityID:  events.AuthenticationActivityIDLogon,
    // ...
}

// Dispatch unknown events by class_uid
decoded, err := events.UnmarshalEvent(data) // e.g. *events.Authentication

// Validate against the embedded compiled schema
v := validate.New(ocsfdata.MustSchema())
result := v.ValidateEvent(data)

See the repository README for full usage, including signing and verifying events under the record_integrity profile.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: ocsf-lake is the datastore/application layer built on this module: storage, querying, ingest-time validation and attestation, and integrity check orchestration.

docs.title: Release Notes v0.1.0
docs.text: Release Date: October 13, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This is the initial release of ocsf-schema-go, the Go implementation of the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF). It compiles OCSF's metaschema source format, generates idiomatic Go bindings for every event class and object, validates events against the real schema semantics, and implements the cryptography of the record_integrity profile.

The module contains no storage or application logic; persistence and ingestion belong in downstream modules such as github.com/grokify/ocsf-lake.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
go get github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go@v0.1.0

To regenerate the bindings from an OCSF checkout:

go run github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go/cmd/ocsfgen@v0.1.0 generate \
  --schema-dir /path/to/ocsf-schema \
  --out ocsf \
  --extension-dirs ocsfext/integrity

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Complete OCSF 1.10.0-dev bindings, including the win, linux, and macos platform extensions
  • Semantic validator driven by an embedded compiled schema, requiring no OCSF checkout at runtime
  • record_integrity signing, verification, and tamper-evident chaining

docs.title: Schema compiler (schema)
docs.text: Loads an OCSF source tree and compiles it: extends flattening, $include profiles, dictionary type joins, platform extensions, external extension roots, class-UID computation, and observable enum synthesis.

docs.title: Generated bindings (ocsf/events, ocsf/objects, ocsf/ocsfdata)
docs.text:
• Structs for every event class and object; attributes marshal to OCSF snake_case, required attributes unconditionally and others with omitempty
  • Enum constants with per-enum *Captions maps, plus ClassNames, ClassCaptions, and CategoryCaptions
  • Class-UID registry: NewEventByClassUID and UnmarshalEvent
  • Observable type registries: ObservableTypeIDBy{Attribute,DictionaryType,Object}
  • Embedded compiled schema (indented JSON) via ocsfdata.MustSchema()

docs.title: Validator (validate)
docs.text:
Checks profile-aware required attributes, scalar types, enum membership, nested objects, at_least_one/just_one constraints, and class_uid/category_uid/type_uid consistency.

v := validate.New(ocsfdata.MustSchema())
result := v.ValidateEvent(eventJSON)
if !result.Valid() {
    for _, issue := range result.Errors() {
        log.Println(issue)
    }
}

docs.title: Record integrity (recordintegrity)
docs.text:
• JCS (RFC 8785) canonicalization and SHA-256 fingerprints; content fingerprints exclude attestation_list, chain fingerprints include it
  • ECDSA and RSA attestation signing with signer certificate metadata
  • Verification with a status taxonomy: verified, unsigned, fingerprint_mismatch, signature_invalid, cert_untrusted, cert_expired, chain_broken, malformed
  • Tamper-evident chain-link verification via VerifyLink

docs.title: Integrity extension (ocsfext/integrity)
docs.text: OCSF 1.10.0-dev defines digital_signature metadata but no attribute for the signature bytes. This extension adds digital_signature.signature_value and will be retired once upstream ocsf-schema#1698 lands an official attribute.

docs.title: Code generator (gen, cmd/ocsfgen)
docs.text: The ocsfgen CLI regenerates the bindings from any OCSF schema checkout, with --extensions for platform extension selection and --extension-dirs for external extension roots.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• The validator does not check regex, range, or max_len facets of dictionary types
  • Generation is not yet pinned to tagged OCSF releases; the schema is generated from the unreleased 1.10.0-dev because the record_integrity profile is absent from stable releases

See docs/specs/ROADMAP.md for planned work.

docs.title: Release Notes v0.2.0
docs.text: Release Date: October 29, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A release that makes events built with the generated types validate strictly as they are produced. It fixes four places where the compiled schema, the generated bindings or the validator differed from how the OCSF schema server presents OCSF.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go@v0.2.0

docs.title: Fixes
docs.text:
• Unused profiles are not written as null. Attributes a profile mixes in, such as cloud and osint, are required only when the event declares the profile in metadata.profiles. They now carry omitempty, so an event without the profile no longer contains "cloud": null and "osint": null.
  • Enums keep Unknown and Other. A class or object that lists its own values for an enum attribute now refines the inherited enum instead of replacing it, from the dictionary through each ancestor to the class. authentication.activity_id is 0–7 and 99, status_id is 0, 1, 2 and 99, and managed_entity.type_id is 0–7 and 99, matching the OCSF schema server. Events using 0 or 99 validate, and the generated ...Unknown and ...Other constants exist for every such attribute.
  • unmapped holds any keys. The validator checked the generic object type (unmapped, xattributes) as an object with no attributes, so with WithUnknownAttributes(UnknownError) every key inside unmapped was an error. It now accepts any keys there and still requires a JSON object.
  • Base Event is a class. base_event is concrete with class_uid 0 and category_uid 0, as the OCSF schema server lists it. ClassUIDBaseEvent is generated, the class registry includes it, and ValidateEvent dispatches events with class_uid 0. Category bases such as iam stay abstract.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
• JSON produced from the generated types no longer contains cloud or osint when they are unset. Code that set them is unaffected.
  • The validator accepts values it rejected before (0 and 99 on refined enums, keys inside unmapped, class_uid 0). A pipeline that relied on those rejections should check its inputs another way.
  • The bindings are regenerated from the same OCSF schema (1.10.0-dev) as v0.1.0.

docs.title: PLAN — ocsf-schema-go
docs.text:
Execution order for Phase 1 (see ROADMAP.md):

  1. Scaffold — go mod init github.com/grokify/ocsf-schema-go, specs, repo hygiene.
  2. schema package — raw types + Load, then Compile (extends → $include → dictionary join → UID computation). Fixture-driven tests first (schema/testdata/minischema), then an opt-in full-tree test gated on OCSF_SCHEMA_DIR pointing at a real ocsf/ocsf-schema checkout.
  3. gen package — naming table, type mapping, template-free emission via strings.Builder + go/format. Unit tests for naming/type edge cases.
  4. cmd/ocsfgen — Cobra CLI: ocsfgen generate --schema-dir <path> --out <dir> --package ocsf.
  5. Generate + verify — run against the local OCSF checkout, commit output under ocsf/, add marshal/unmarshal round-trip tests, golangci-lint run, coverage badge.
  6. Docs + commits — README, conventional topical commits (feat schema, feat gen, feat cli, feat generated bindings, test, docs, chore).

Key risks handled up front:

  • $include inside attribute maps breaks naive decoding → decode attributes as map[string]json.RawMessage.
  • Name collisions after case conversion (e.g. _resource vs resource_details) → hidden objects are never emitted; enum caption collisions get numeric suffixes.
  • omitempty dropping meaningful false → booleans generate as *bool.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) defines a vendor-agnostic event taxonomy for security telemetry. The schema is authored in OCSF's own JSON metaschema format (not standard JSON Schema): event classes and objects use extends inheritance, $include profile mixins, and attribute types resolved from a shared dictionary.json. Go programs that produce or consume OCSF events today must either hand-write structs or depend on protobuf-generated bindings that don't marshal to idiomatic OCSF JSON.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. Generated Go structs for every OCSF object and event class, marshaling directly to spec-compliant OCSF JSON (snake_case attribute names, correct optionality).
  2. Enum constants for classification values (class_uid, category_uid, activity_id, type_id, severity_id, …) with captions preserved in doc comments.
  3. Schema-compilation library (schema package) that loads an OCSF schema source tree and resolves inheritance, profiles, and dictionary types — usable independently of the code generator (e.g., for validators, doc tooling, mapping tools).
  4. Regenerable: a ocsfgen CLI re-generates the bindings from any OCSF schema checkout, so the library can track upstream releases.

docs.title: Non-Goals (v0)
docs.text:
• OCSF platform extensions (extensions/windows, linux, macos).
  • Runtime validation (constraints such as at_least_one, regex/range checks).
  • The OCSF server "compiled schema" export format (/export/schema).

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
• Go services emitting OCSF events (SIEM pipelines, log producers).
  • Go consumers parsing OCSF events (analytics, normalization, routing).
  • Tooling authors needing programmatic access to the OCSF schema definition itself.

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text:
schema/         Metaschema parsing + compilation (source of truth for semantics)
validate/       Semantic validator driven by a compiled schema
gen/            Go code generation from a compiled schema
cmd/ocsfgen/    Thin Cobra CLI over gen
ocsf/objects/   Generated object structs + observable registries (committed)
ocsf/events/    Generated event structs, constants, class-UID registry (committed)
ocsf/ocsfdata/  Generated embedded compiled schema (indented JSON + go:embed accessor)

docs.title: OCSF source format (input)
docs.text:
An OCSF schema checkout contains:

  • version.json — schema semver.
  • categories.json — category name → {uid, caption, description}.
  • dictionary.json — ~1000 attribute definitions; each has a type that is either a scalar type key from dictionary.json#/types/attributes (string_t, integer_t, long_t, timestamp_t, boolean_t, float_t, json_t, plus string/int subtypes such as ip_t, port_t, email_t) or the name of an object. is_array: true marks array attributes. Untyped usages default per attribute name via the dictionary.
  • objects/*.json — object definitions. extends names a parent object (object is the implicit empty root). Names beginning with _ (_entity, _resource) are hidden (abstract): they exist only to be extended.
  • events/**/*.json — event class definitions. extends chains terminate at base_event. A class with a top-level uid is concrete: class_uid = category_uid × 1000 + uid; category bases without uid are abstract. base_event has no uid either but is concrete: the OCSF schema server lists it as Base Event, class_uid 0 in category other (category_uid 0), for events that fit no other class. type_uid = class_uid × 100 + activity_id.
  • profiles/*.json — attribute mixins pulled in via "$include": [paths] inside an attributes map (the only $include shape used in the repo).

Attribute entries inside objects/events/profiles are partial overrides: the dictionary supplies type/is_array/caption, the local entry supplies/overrides requirement, description, enum, group, @deprecated.

docs.title: schema package
docs.text:
• Load(dir string) (*Schema, error) — reads the tree into raw definitions.
  • (*Schema).Compile() (*CompiledSchema, error) — produces flattened definitions:
  • Resolve $include profiles into the including entity's attribute map.
  • Walk extends chains (child overrides parent attribute-by-attribute; property-level merge: non-zero child fields win; a child enum is merged into the parent enum, the child winning on the same value, from the dictionary through each ancestor to the class, matching upstream server behavior, so classes keep 0 Unknown and 99 Other).
  • Join each attribute against the dictionary for type, is_array, default caption and description.
  • Compute ClassUID for concrete classes.
  • Attribute maps parse via map[string]json.RawMessage to lift $include out before decoding Attribute values.
  • Hidden objects (_-prefixed) are compiled (they are extension bases) but flagged Hidden: true so the generator can skip emitting them.

docs.title: gen package
docs.text:
• Type mapping: boolean_t → *bool; integer_t & int subtypes → int; long_t/timestamp_t → int64; float_t → float64; json_t → any; string family → string; object types → *T (or []T when is_array); the generic object type → map[string]any. Scalar arrays → []elem.
  • Optionality: attributes with requirement: required marshal always, except attributes a profile mixes in (required only when the event declares the profile); all others get ,omitempty. Booleans are *bool so false survives marshaling.
  • Naming: snake_case → PascalCase with an initialism table (ID, UID, URL, IP, OS, TLS, DNS, HTTP, API, CVE, CVSS, …). Hidden-object names never surface. Enum constant names: <Type><Field><Caption> with caption sanitized to a Go identifier; collisions get the numeric value appended.
  • Enums: emitted as untyped int constants grouped per attribute, plus a ClassUID/CategoryUID constant per concrete class/category.
  • Output is gofmt-formatted via go/format before writing.

docs.title: ocsf package (generated)
docs.text:
• One file per event category (events_iam.go, …), objects.go, constants.go, version.go (const SchemaVersion).
  • Every struct/field carries doc comments derived from captions/descriptions (HTML stripped).

docs.title: Platform extensions
docs.text:
LoadWithExtensions(dir, names...) ("all" or specific names) loads extensions/<dir>/:

  • extension.json supplies {uid, name}; extension classes get class_uid = extension_uid × 100000 + category_uid × 1000 + uid.
  • Extension dictionary.json entries are additive; redefining a core entry errors.
  • Files with extends but no name are patches: their attributes overlay the extended core definition, $include lists append (extension-relative paths are qualified at load time), and constraints replace.
  • Extension provenance is recorded (Definition.Extension, Attribute.Source = "extension:<name>").

docs.title: Observable enum synthesis
docs.text: The source schema declares only 0/99 in observable.type_id; the full enum is derived (as the OCSF server does) from observable: annotations on dictionary types, dictionary attributes, objects, and object/class attributes, first-writer-wins in that priority order. The generator also emits ObservableTypeIDByAttribute, ObservableTypeIDByDictionaryType, and ObservableTypeIDByObject maps into the objects package.

docs.title: validate package
docs.text:
validate.New(compiledSchema, opts...) builds a class-UID-indexed semantic validator; ValidateEvent dispatches on the payload's class_uid, ValidateEventClass/ValidateObject target a definition by name. Checks:

  • required attributes (profile-sourced requirements apply only when metadata.profiles activates that profile);
  • scalar type conformance by root dictionary type, arrays, nested objects (recursive);
  • enum membership (skipped for class_uid/category_uid/type_uid, which get structural checks instead: class lookup, category match, type_uid = class_uid×100 + activity_id);
  • at_least_one / just_one constraints;
  • unknown attributes (warn by default, configurable) and deprecation warnings.

All findings are Issue{Code, Path, Message, Warning} on a Result; only non-warning issues fail Result.Valid().

docs.title: Generated registries (events package)
docs.text: NewEventByClassUID (switch over ClassUID* constants), UnmarshalEvent (probe class_uid, decode into the concrete struct), ClassNames, ClassCaptions, CategoryCaptions, per-enum <Prefix>Captions maps, and shared SeverityID*/StatusID* constants lifted from base_event.

docs.title: Embedded schema (ocsf/ocsfdata)
docs.text: The generator serializes the entire CompiledSchema to indented JSON (schema.json, ~5.5 MB, uncompressed so it stays scannable and reviewable in diffs) with a go:embed accessor (Schema()/MustSchema(), decoded once behind sync.Once). Attribute.Source serializes as _source so profile/extension provenance survives the round-trip — the validator's profile-aware requirement logic depends on it. Runtime validation needs no OCSF checkout: validate.New(ocsfdata.MustSchema()).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• schema: fixture tree under schema/testdata/minischema exercising extends, $include, dictionary fallback, enum override, hidden objects; plus an opt-in test against a real checkout via OCSF_SCHEMA_DIR.
  • gen: naming and type-mapping unit tests; golden-compile test (generated code for the fixture parses with go/parser).
  • ocsf: round-trip marshal/unmarshal tests against hand-written OCSF JSON samples.

docs.title: Upstream: signature bytes on digital_signature (ocsf-schema #1698)
docs.text: Status: draft — not yet posted. To be posted as a comment on ocsf/ocsf-schema#1698 once this repository is public, so the referenced implementation is verifiable.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
OCSF's record_integrity profile (ocsf/ocsf-schema#1661) lets an event carry cryptographic attestations: an attestation_list whose entries hold the event fingerprint, optional tamper-evident chain references (prev_event, chain_uid), and a signatures array of digital_signature objects. However, digital_signature records only signature metadata (algorithm, certificate reference, serialization scheme, state) — it has no attribute for the signature bytes themselves, which makes self-contained verification impossible. The gap was acknowledged in the #1661 review discussion and deferred to issue #1698, which proposes two candidate designs:

  • Option A — add value plus encoding/encoding_id to digital_signature, mirroring the fingerprint object's pattern.
  • Option B — introduce a wrapper signature object that holds the blob and contains digital_signature as a descriptor.

docs.title: Our position
docs.text: This module implements the profile end to end (see the recordintegrity package and the ocsfext/integrity schema extension, which patches digital_signature with a signature_value attribute as an interim carrier). That experience supports Option A: one additive field on digital_signature proved sufficient for signing, verification, multi-signer attestations, and chain validation, with no need for Option B's extra nesting. When an official attribute lands, the ocsfext/integrity extension will be retired in its favor.

docs.title: Draft comment for #1698
docs.text:
**+1 for Option A** (`value` + `encoding`/`encoding_id` on `digital_signature`), with
implementation experience to back it.

We've built a working record-integrity implementation in Go — canonicalization,
signing, verification, and tamper-evident chain walking over `prev_event` links —
against OCSF main. Since `digital_signature` has no field for the bytes today, we
carried them via a small schema extension that patches `digital_signature` with a
single attribute (`signature_value`, `bytestring_t`, requirement `recommended`),
which is effectively Option A minus the encoding enum. Observations from running it:

- **Option A was sufficient in practice.** One field on `digital_signature` composed
  cleanly with everything already in #1661: `attestation.signatures[]` handled
  multi-signer cases (producer + co-signer) unchanged, `serialization_id` told the
  verifier how to reproduce the signing input (we used JCS/RFC 8785 + SHA-256 over
  the event with `attestation_list` excluded), and per-signature `certificate`
  metadata (SHA-256 fingerprint, issuer + serial) was enough to select the
  verification key. End-to-end verification and hash-chain validation work with no
  additional nesting, which makes Option B's wrapper object feel like structure
  without a payoff.

- **Mirroring the `fingerprint` pattern (`value` + `encoding_id`) is the right
  call.** We hard-coded Base64 and still found ourselves wanting the explicit
  `encoding_id` for symmetry with `fingerprint` — verifiers already have that
  decode path.

- **`recommended` (not `required`) seems right** for the new attribute, since
  `digital_signature` retains its descriptor role for file/Authenticode signatures
  where the bytes legitimately live in the artifact.

One adjacent gap worth noting (possibly its own issue): fully self-contained
verification also needs the signer certificate to be obtainable. The `certificate`
object carries issuer/serial/validity/fingerprints but not the certificate itself,
so a consumer with no prior relationship to the producer still needs an out-of-band
cert store — echoing the PKCS#7 point raised in the #1661 review. A `data`/`pem`
attribute on `certificate` (or a defined external-reference convention) would close
that loop; happy to open a separate issue if useful.

If Option A lands, we'll drop our extension and align with the official attribute.
Happy to share the implementation once we publish it, or draft the schema PR for
Option A if that helps move this along.

docs.title: Post-landing checklist (when an official attribute exists)
docs.text:
1. Update ocsfext/integrity (or remove it) and regenerate the ocsf/ bindings.
  2. Rename SignatureValue usage in recordintegrity (sign + verify paths) to the official attribute; add encoding_id handling if Option A lands with the enum.
  3. Regenerate ocsf/ocsfdata so the embedded schema and validator accept the official attribute.
  4. Update ocsf-lake (pkg/integrity, ocsflake sign/verify) and both READMEs.
